findings.location: design.md#Decision: Customers are merged by e-mail
findings.recommendation: The load-bearing fact "an e-mail address identifies exactly one person" is refuted by design.md#Context: "Business customers often share a purchasing mailbox (`orders@acme.example`) between several buyers, each with their own customer record and billing address." Scenario: buyers A (oldest) and B both use orders@acme.example; the nightly job moves B's orders to A and deletes B, so B's orders are billed to A's address and B no longer exists. Choose a key that holds for that case (e.g. e-mail plus name/billing address, or merge only records created by guest checkout as the Why describes — the schema in app/schema.sql has no column telling guests apart, so the plan must say how), or exclude shared mailboxes explicitly. Add a spec scenario "Two buyers share a mailbox → both records remain", and align the requirement with the design's case-insensitive matching ("share an e-mail address" vs "lower-cased e-mail").
findings.title: The merge key rests on an assumption the design's own context contradicts

findings.evidence: moves the others' orders to it and deletes the others.
findings.location: design.md#Decision: Customers are merged by e-mail
findings.recommendation: The deletion is irreversible: the deleted records' name and billing_address (app/schema.sql) are lost and the moved orders can no longer be traced back to their original customer, so a wrong merge (see R-skeptic-1) cannot be undone. Keep a trace before deleting (soft delete, or a merge log mapping old id → kept id with the original fields), or stage the rollout (dry-run report first), and state the rollback in the design and a task.
findings.title: Duplicate records are deleted with no way back

findings.evidence: A nightly job SHALL merge customer records that share an e-mail address into the oldest one, moving their orders to it.
findings.recommendation: The only scenarios are "Two records, one e-mail" and "No duplicate". Missing: e-mails differing only by case; records with the same e-mail but different names or billing addresses (which one's data survives); two records with the same created_at (which is "the oldest"); a guest checkout inserting a customer or order while the job runs. Add a scenario for each, and extend task 1.1's tests to them.
findings.title: The spec covers only the happy path

findings.recommendation: The change adds "A nightly job" (proposal.md#What Changes) that must be scheduled, run and monitored, and that deletes production rows, yet the operations domain is unticked with no reason, so no expert reviews how it is deployed, scheduled or watched. Tick operations, or give the reason on its line.
findings.title: A scheduled job is added with operations unticked and no reason
